@@ -0,0 +1,198 @@ +--- +title: "ADR-042: Three typed borrows from Tera/Zola — numeric predicates, `~` concat, typed inline signatures" +sidebar: + label: ADR-042 numeric predicates, ~concat, typed inline +--- + +*Status:* **Accepted** (surface frozen here; implemented smallest-first — see §7). *Date:* 2026-06-11. +Applies to the **MaxBars** surface (the PureScript reference / oracle for the Trussbars production +engine) and its two backends — the AOT Rust emitter (`MaxBars.Rust` → `trussbars-std`) and the VM +(`trussbars-vm`). Builds on the prelude single-source rule +([catalog convention](/concepts/)) and the dialect ladder of +[ADR-005](/adr/adr-0005-dialect-ladder/); follows the discipline that *author-facing surface syntax +is frozen in an ADR before the implementation PR*. + +## 1. Context + +The northstar survey ([`trussbars/docs/24-northstar-migration.md`](https://codeberg.org)) put **Zola +(Tera)** as the lead migration target, which prompted a feature-by-feature comparison of Tera/Zola +against MaxBars/Trussbars. Three Tera/Jinja constructs have no MaxBars equivalent *yet* but map +cleanly onto the typed, fixed-vocabulary, injection-safe model — and each is **more** idiomatic in +Trussbars than in its source language *because* Trussbars is typed: + +1. **Numeric predicates.** Tera/Jinja spell `if n is even` / `is odd` / `is divisible_by(3)`. MaxBars + already ships the *membership* and *affix* predicates (`includes`, `startsWith`, `endsWith`) but + has **no numeric-parity predicate** — you must write `(eq (modulo n 2) 0)` by hand. +2. **String concatenation.** Tera/Jinja/Twig spell concatenation with the `~` operator. MaxBars has + **no concatenation operator** at all (you reach for the `append`/`prepend` helpers). Because the + northstar is a **Zola/Tera migration**, MaxBars adopts Tera's exact `~` spelling — a ported + template's `name ~ "!"` reads unchanged — while the typed engine removes the *reason* `~` exists in + Jinja (disambiguating an overloaded `+`): here `~` is the *only* concat spelling and `+` stays + strictly numeric. +3. **Macros with signatures.** Tera's `{% macro card(title, badge="") %}` are *untyped* — a wrong + call is a runtime error. MaxBars already has parameterised partials (`{% inline "card" %}` + + `{% include "card" title=x %}`, the hash merges onto the partial context), but **no declared + parameter list** — so there is no arity/spelling contract and no place to hang AOT types. + +This ADR freezes the surface for all three. It deliberately picks the *fixed-vocabulary* shape over +new sigils wherever the prelude can carry the meaning (predicates), and reuses existing machinery +(the include-hash for inline parameters) rather than inventing a call syntax. + +## 2. Decision — numeric predicates as prelude value operations + +Add three **value operations** to `Kernel.Prelude` (the single source — the catalog, the VM, and the +AOT emitter all derive from it): + +| Operation | Arity | Meaning | Desugars from | +| --- | --- | --- | --- | +| `even` | unary | `True` when the number is even | call `(even n)` / pipe `n \| even` | +| `odd` | unary | `True` when the number is odd | call `(odd n)` / pipe `n \| odd` | +| `divisibleBy` | binary | `True` when the first number is divisible by the second | call `(divisibleBy n 3)` / pipe `n \| divisibleBy 3` | + +They are plain operations — **no `is` infix sugar** (rejected in §5). They read naturally in both the +output and guard positions MaxBars already supports (in a block head a helper application is +parenthesised, MaxBars' existing rule — a bare pipe there collides with block-param syntax): + +```truss +{{ n | even }} {# output: "true" / "false" #} +{% if (n | even) %}even{% elif (divisibleBy n 3) %}fizz{% endif %} +``` + +- **Type:** both consume `Number`, produce `Bool`. A non-number is a `TypeError` (same rule as the + arithmetic operations — no string coercion, deterministic across backends). +- **`even`/`odd`** are defined against the same `jsMod` used by `modulo`, so `even n ≡ eq (modulo n 2) 0` + bit-for-bit on every backend. `odd` is `not even` (never a second parity computation, so the two + can't drift). +- **`divisibleBy n d`** is `eq (modulo n d) 0`. `d = 0` follows `modulo`'s existing `d = 0` behaviour + (no new edge rule). + +The names are MaxBars-canonical (camelCase `divisibleBy`, matching `startsWith`/`endsWith`); the +Tera/Jinja spelling `divisible_by` is **not** an alias (MaxBars has never mirrored snake_case +spellings — see `startsWith`, not `starts_with`). + +## 3. Decision — `~` is the string concatenation operator (Tera's spelling; no `+` overload) + +A new infix operator `~` joins MaxBars at **additive precedence** (beside `+`/`-`), desugaring to a +new prelude operation `concat` — the same spelling and meaning as Tera/Jinja: + +| Left | Right | `~` means | Result | +| --- | --- | --- | --- | +| `String` | `String` | concatenation | `String` | +| mixed (e.g. `String ~ Number`) | | **error** | — | + +`+` stays **strictly numeric** — it is *not* overloaded. Concatenation lives on its own operator so +the two never have to be disambiguated by their operand types at a glance, and `+`'s byte-identical +numeric codegen is untouched. Adopting Tera's `~` (rather than an `+` overload or the +Haskell-flavoured `++`) is a deliberate **migration** choice: a Zola/Tera template's `~` ports +verbatim. Where Jinja's `~` exists to *paper over* an ambiguous overloaded `+` (so `"1" ~ 1 == "11"` +coerces silently), MaxBars keeps the `~` spelling but **not** the coercion — mixed/non-string operands +are a `TypeError`, surfacing the bug the typed engine can see. + +- **Lexer:** MaxBars (which owns its front-end, [ADR-041](/adr/adr-0041-per-surface-lexer-parser/)) + lexes `~` as the operator token `TOp "~"` (a new entry in MaxBars' operator set). +- **Parser:** `MaxBars.Expr` parses `a ~ b` at the additive rung into `concat a b` (left-assoc, like + `+`). +- **Oracle (PureScript):** `concat` is a binary operation — two `VString` → `VString`; any other + operand pairing is a `TypeError` (no coercion, deterministic across backends, same discipline as + the arithmetic operations). +- **VM:** the `("concat", [a,b])` dispatch mirrors the oracle — two strings concatenate, else + `TypeError`. +- **AOT (typed):** `concat` emits `trussbars_std::concat(&a, &b) -> String`. Because the emitted + helper takes string references, a non-string operand is a **Rust compile error** — AOT rejects at + build time exactly what the oracle/VM reject at render time, with no type information threaded into + the emitter. + +The existing `append`/`prepend` *affix* helpers stay (fixed argument order, a different ergonomic from +the symmetric operator). Concatenation of more than two pieces chains naturally (`a ~ b ~ c`). Array +concatenation is a **natural future extension** of `~` (sequence concat) but is out of scope here — +`~` is string-only for this increment (strings are ~all template concatenation), and widening it +later is additive. + +## 4. Decision — typed `{% inline %}` signatures + +An `{% inline %}` definition may declare a **parameter list** after its name: + +```truss +{% inline "card" (title, badge="") %} +

{{ title }}

{% if badge %}{{ badge }}{% endif %}
+{% endinline %} + +{% include "card" title=post.name badge="new" %} +{% include "card" title=post.name %} {# badge defaults to "" #} +``` + +The signature is `( name ( , name ( = default )? )* )` — comma-separated parameter names, each with an +optional default that is a **literal** (string/number/bool/null) or another in-scope nullary operation +value. The body binds each parameter as a **local** sourced from the matching `{% include %}` hash +argument; a parameter with no matching hash arg falls back to its default, and a parameter with +**neither** a hash arg nor a default is a located error at the include site (the typed-macro contract +Tera lacks). + +- **Surface parse:** `MaxBars.Parser`'s inline-head parser (MaxBars owns its front-end per + [ADR-041](/adr/adr-0041-per-surface-lexer-parser/)) gains an optional `( … )` after the partial + name. The empty signature `{% inline "x" %}` is unchanged (no list = today's "merge the whole + include hash" behaviour, preserved for back-compat). +- **Desugar / binding:** a signed inline desugars to the body wrapped so each declared parameter + resolves to `hash-arg ?? default`, scoping the names as locals (the existing `{% include %}` hash + already lands on the partial context — the signature *names and bounds* what it carries, rather + than changing how it is passed). +- **AOT typing (the differentiator):** the schema-inference pass (`inferMax`) reads the signature to + type each parameter from its call-site argument (and checks the default's type agrees), so a + missing required argument or a type-mismatched argument is a **compile-time** error — a typed macro, + which Tera's untyped `{% macro %}` cannot offer. +- **Call syntax is unchanged:** `{% include "card" k=v %}` already exists (ADR-039 §5.7); the + signature adds the *declaration* side only. No new call keyword (`{% call %}` etc.) is introduced. + +Required-vs-optional is positional-free (every argument is a named hash key), so reordering and +partial application read the same as today; the signature only adds the *names + defaults + types*. + +## 5. Rejected alternatives + +- **`is even` / `is divisible_by(n)` infix (Tera/Jinja "tests").** Rejected: a new `is` keyword + a + test namespace duplicates the operation vocabulary for one read-aloud nicety. MaxBars already reads + cleanly with the pipe (`n | even`) and the call (`even n`), both of which reuse the *one* fixed + operation vocabulary (ADR-019) the catalog, hover, and linter already know. A bespoke `is` grammar + would need its own paint, its own diagnostics, and its own catalog projection for zero new meaning. +- **Overloading `+` for concat (type-directed `+`).** Rejected in favour of the dedicated `~`: a + separate operator is clearer at a glance (no "is this `+` numeric or string?"), keeps `+`'s numeric + codegen byte-identical, and avoids monomorphising a `Plus` trait. +- **`++` for concat (Haskell/Elm/Gleam spelling).** Considered, but rejected in favour of Tera's `~`: + the northstar is a Zola/Tera migration, so matching Tera's operator verbatim lets ported templates' + `~` carry over unchanged — the migration parity outweighs `~`'s general unfamiliarity (and `~` here + is *less* surprising than in Jinja, since it can never silently coerce). +- **`{% macro %}` / `{% call %}` as a new construct.** Rejected: `{% inline %}` + `{% include k=v %}` + already *is* the parameterised-partial machinery; adding a parallel macro construct would fork the + partial registry and the include path for no capability the signature (§4) doesn't already give. +- **Positional macro arguments (`{% include "card" x y %}`).** Rejected: MaxBars partials are + context-merge, not positional-apply; named hash args are the established, reorder-safe call shape. + +## 6. Consequences + +- **One new vocabulary increment.** Four operations (`even`/`odd`/`divisibleBy` + the `~`-backing + `concat`) enter the prelude, so `gen:catalog` / `gen:operations` regenerate and the catalog, LSP + hover, and TextMate/`operations.json` painter pick them up for free (the single-source rule pays + off). The inline signature adds **no** new operation name. `~` is a new operator token but reuses + the existing infix-desugar machinery. +- **Backends stay in lockstep.** Each addition lands in all three of oracle / AOT / VM and is pinned by + the trussbars conformance harness (oracle ≡ AOT ≡ VM, byte-identical) plus a `test:compile` case — + no backend can drift. +- **AOT gains a genuinely typed macro** (§4) — a Zola/Tera migration headline: "same templates, but a + wrong macro call is a *compile* error." +- **No new runtime primitive.** Predicates and `concat` are prelude operations; `~` is sugar for + `concat`; inline signatures desugar to existing local-binding + include-hash machinery. Nothing new to the engine + core or the VM opcode set. + +## 7. Implementation order (smallest-first) + +1. **Numeric predicates** — `Kernel.Prelude` (`even`/`odd`/`divisibleBy`) + `MaxBars.Rust` call-table + + `trussbars-std` (`even`/`odd`/`divisible_by`) + `trussbars-vm` dispatch + `gen:catalog`/ + `gen:operations` + conformance cases + MaxBars tests. +2. **`~` concat** — the `concat` operation in the oracle + VM; the `~` token in `MaxBars.Lexer` + and the additive-rung parse in `MaxBars.Expr`; `trussbars_std::concat` and the `concat` emit in + `MaxBars.Rust`; `gen:catalog`/`gen:operations`; conformance + `test:compile` cases. +3. **Typed `{% inline %}` signatures** — `MaxBars.Parser` head, the binding desugar, the `inferMax` + typing, the include-site arity/type check; conformance + tests; `engine/maxbars.mdx` + the + `/maxbars` tutorial. + +Each is a self-contained, separately-committed, fully-green increment (the surface is frozen here, so +no spelling churn mid-implementation).
